A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable text, equations, figures, Table 1, and Appendices A–G. Retained, revised, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic ERM simulations, empirical score distributions and error curves, and MNIST classification results in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation and MNIST results and reports additional empirical results for the elastic-loss experiment in Figures 1 and 3.

M1.justification: The ERM procedure, quadratic-surrogate construction in Section 3, deterministic min–max objective, and fixed-point system remain unchanged. The elastic-loss experiment evaluates the existing framework; the changes to displayed mathematical expressions are formal corrections rather than a new algorithm.

E1.justification: The synthetic binary-classification demonstration in v1 Figure 1 is replaced by a bimodal teacher–student regression experiment. Synthetic regression was already covered by v1 Figure 2, so this is a limited reshaping of coverage. MNIST classification using digits {3,6} versus {4,7} remains unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparison approaches remain Gaussian-score approximations and moment-matched Gaussian-data surrogates. The retained MNIST experiment has the same comparator lineup. The new loss experiment does not introduce another comparison method.

E3.justification: The new regression experiment uses p = 30 and n = 50 and sweeps eta from 0 to 1 in the loss (1−eta)ℓ2 + etaℓ1. This adds a loss-sweep protocol; it does not establish that the retained MNIST or regularizer-orientation experiments were rerun under changed settings.

E4.justification: Figures 1 and 3 add a sensitivity study of how Gaussian universality and fixed-point parameters vary with the loss. Figure 4 also adds the full Gaussian-convolved score prediction to the retained regularizer-orientation diagnostic. The MNIST and subspace-confinement analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies experimental seeds or repeated-run counts or reports empirical confidence intervals or significance tests. The revised figures do not introduce uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The replacement Figure 1 reports regression errors of approximately 3.4 for bimodal data and 2.9 for its Gaussian surrogate at eta = 1; Figure 3 adds fixed-point parameter curves. Appendix F’s illustrated projection onto F changes from bimodal in v1 Figure 3 to single-peaked in v2 Figure 5, without an explained setting change. MNIST results are retained. These are new or revised results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation (3) gains a factor of 1/2. Claim 4.1 revises the auxiliary objective’s vector pairings and covariance-weighted norm, removing dimensional inconsistencies in the earlier expression. The principal theorem statements, fixed-point equations, and appendix proofs otherwise remain substantively unchanged; no proof accompanies the newly announced work on Assumption 4.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims: quadratic regularizer universality, non-Gaussian ERM asymptotics, Gaussian-convolved test scores, and subspace confinement. The additional experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly calls Claim 4.1 a conjecture and states that a proof of minimizer universality is under preparation. Its new Figure 1 caption also introduces ambiguity: it says performance and score universality are satisfied only at eta = 0 while showing non-Gaussian scores there and subsequently explaining that Gaussian scores are unnecessary for performance universality.

D1.justification: The code-access pointer changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. v2 also supplies p = 30, n = 50, and the loss-interpolation formula for its new experiment. These additions do not establish changed implementation settings for retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chatterjee (2008) and Shao and Zhang (2025) to identify a proposed approach to proving minimizer universality. The broader research positioning and Table 1 comparison remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a paper roadmap in Section 1.3 and explanatory paragraphs after Theorem 4.3, edits grammar and author affiliations, and adds acknowledgements. The main section and appendix organization remains stable. Some introductory descriptions of the replaced Figure 1 were not updated.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially revised: Figure 1 is replaced, a fixed-point plot is added as Figure 3, and the MNIST figure moves from Appendix G into the main text as Figure 2. The regularizer and confinement figures are redrawn with revised legends, curves, and formatting. Table 1 is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 repairs the auxiliary objective, makes its conjectural status clearer, and adds useful explanations and loss diagnostics. However, the new Figure 1 introduces ambiguity about the paper’s central distinction between score and performance universality, while the introduction still describes the removed classification panels. Appendix F also changes a displayed distribution without explaining the setting. These gains and interpretive problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
